newsitem.title: TAIWAN: President says inquiry, listing delay unrelated.
newsitem.headline: President says inquiry, listing delay unrelated.

text.p: Taiwan's President Enterprises said on Tuesday there was no link between its unit President Securities, facing an insider trading inquiry, and its President Chain Store delaying its Tuesday share listing.

"From the parent company's point of view, we can say for certain the operations of President Securities and President Chain Store are completely independent of each other, and their affairs do not relate," President Enterprises' spokesman Yang Yu-pao told Reuters by telephone.
Yang would not comment further on a government inquiry into possible insider trading at President Securities.
The Securities and Exchange Commission said the initial public stock offering for President Chain Store has been delayed indefinitely.
In the same statement, the agency said it was investigating President Securities for possible insider trading.
It did not say whether the cases were connected.
President Enterprises had planned on Tuesday to release up to T$2 billion of its shares in President Chain Store.
The company, which runs the 7-ELEVEN franchise in Taiwan, had been scheduled for listing at the end of 1996.
President Enterprises said it did not know when the stock offering for President Chain Store would be rescheduled.
"The first thing we have to do is clarify to the Securities and Exchange Commission that the insider trading could not possibly involve President Chain Store," Yang said.
"From there, it is the commission's decision whether to let us go ahead with the offering," he said.
